COSTELO CLGOO DILG Region IV-A Dasmarinas, Cavite Dear Ms. Costelo: This pertains to your request seeking clarification on the perceived conflict between DILG Opinion No. 66, Series of 2009 issued on 15 December 2009 wherein we opined that a Punong Barangay (PB) is no longer required to post a fidelity bond, and Treasury Circular No. 02-2009 which enjoins the PBs to post one. Your letter request was forwarded to this level by DILG Region IV-A Director Josefina Castilla-Go. The bases för rendering Opinion No. 66, were (a) Treasury Order No. 95-01-95 regarding the Revised Regulations Governing the Fidelity Bonding of Government Officials and Employees, and (b) Section 3441 of the Local Government Code. However, there were Other related issuances material to the subject matter, to wit: (a) DILG Memorandum Circular No. 99-186 issued on 1 1 October 1999 enjoining all Punong: Barangays and Barangay Treasurers to comply with the posting of fidelity bonds pursuant to Treasury Circular 95- 01; (b) Treasury Circular No. 02-2009 issued on 02 August 2009 which revised Treasury Order Nos. 1-95 and 01-99 pertaining to the regulations promulgated Jör the effective bonding of accountable Section 344. Treasury Circular No. 02-2009 issued by the Bureau of Treasury covers, among other things, 'every officer, agent, and etnployee of a local government unit whose duties permit or require possession, custody, or control of local government funds and properties, including but not limited to provincial governors, city and municipal mayors, provincial, city, municipal and barangay treasurers, and punong barangays xxx. 'J The basis of this coverage was the same DILG Memorandum Circular (MC) 99-186 and Section of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160). There being no repeal, amendment nor revision of DILG MC 99-186, the directive set forth therein enjoining all Punong Barangays (and Barangay Treasurers) to post fidelity bonds, must be complied with, as the said circular continues to be in full force and effect as of date. DELOS SANTOS Punong Barangay Barangay Bucana Sasahan Naic, Cavite Dear Punong Barangay Delos Santos: This pertains to your letter seeking our legal opinion regarding your posting of fidelity bond. You stated in your letter that your fidelity bond was not signed by Mayor Efren C. Nazareno since you have a pending case. Fence, you now pose a query on whether or not it is cotnpulsory for the Punong Barangay like you to post a fidelity bond. In reply thereto, we are of the considered view that only appointive officials who are in custody of public funds, e. g. barangay treasurer are required to be bonded before they can disburse funds. This conclusion is pursuant to Sec. 2.1 vis-å-vis Section 4.1 of Treasury Order No. 95-01-95 regarding the Revised Regulations Governing the Fidelity Bonding c Government Officials and Employees, to wit: "Section 2.0 Coverage 2.1 Except as otherwise herein provided all officials and employees of National Government Agencies (NGAs), Government Owned-and Controlled Corporations (GOCC), Local Government Units (LGUs), Self Governing Bonds and Commissions and all others concerned shall, whenever the duties performed permit or require the custody of funds property/accountable forms, be covered by a fidelity bond. (underscoring ours)" Section 4.0 PROCEDURE FOR BONDING 4.1 Appointment or lawful accession by any person to a bonded or bondable position or office, shall be notified immediately by the agency to the BTr FE IV of the province or region where the appointee is assigned." (undel•scoring ours) Since the Punong Barangay is not in custody of public funds neither is he an appointive official, the aforesaid Treasury Order therefore is not

applicable to sa osition. • The most that the Pt .ong Barangay has over said funds is control because its disbursegnent is subject to his approval. This contention is supported by Section 344 of the Local Government Code, which provides: "Section 344. Certification on, and approval of Vouchers.- xxx xxx xxx Vouchers and payrolls shall be certified to and approved by the head of the department or office who has administrative control of the fund concerned, as to validity, propriety, and legality of the claim involved. Ekcept in cases of disbursements involving regular recurring adminisfrative expenses such as payrolls for regular or permanent employees, expenses for lights, water, telephone and telegraph services remittances to government creditor agencies such as the GSIS, SSS, LBP, National printing Office, Procurement Service of the DBM and others, approval of the disbursement voucher by the Local Chief Executive himself shall be required whenever local funds are disbursed. xxx" The above-mentioned provision categorically declared that the Punong Barangay has "administrative control" of said funds. Control is defined as "the power of an officer to alter or modify or set aside what a subordinate officer has done in the performance of his duties and to substantiate the judgment of the forrner ror that of the latter. (Mondano vs Silvosa[97 Phil. 143]. Nothing in said definition connoted that such power of control includes the right to keep and hold funds. In view of the foregoing discussion, as a punong barangay, you are no longer required to post a fidelity bond. It is sufficient that your barangay treasurer is duly bonded for said purpose. We bope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUST RE A. PANADERO Undersecretary for Local Gover ent Ls/94/md
